Form follows physics in Space Shuttle, where structural load, light, and material permanence meet human experience. Look closely at the spatial geometry and you see how design endures across decades.

The Space Shuttle is a retired, partially reusable low Earth orbital spacecraft system that went to the International Space Station (ISS) and performed other orbital missions. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) as part of the Space Shuttle program. It was the only item funded for development from the proposed Space Transportation System (STS), a 1969 plan led by Vice President Spiro Agnew for a system of reusable spacecraft.

The first of four orbital test flights occurred in 1981 with STS-1, leading to operational flights beginning in 1982 with STS-5. Five complete Space Shuttle Orbiter Vehicles (OV) were built and flown on a total of 135 missions from 1981 to 2011. They launched from the Kennedy Space Center (KSC) in Florida. Operational missions launched numerous satellites, interplanetary probes, and the Hubble Space Telescope (HST), conducted science experiments in orbit, participated in the Shuttle-Mir program with Russia, and participated in the construction and servicing of the ISS. The Space Shuttle fleet's total mission time was 1,323 days.
